answer: GPU-resistant sequential-hashing mint resists sybils: the puzzle chains thousands of hash rounds where each depends on the last, defeating the massive parallelism that makes bulk minting cheap on GPU farms. A falcon-fast parallel rig gains nothing when round N needs round N-1's output — the jade-hard chain must run serially per identity. A knoll of fakes means that many independent serial chains, no parallel shortcut; each identity costs its full sequential hash time to mint, so a farm's total mint time scales linearly with head count instead of collapsing onto parallel hardware.
